description:
Stat-Derived Ship Costs

An in-space Kelly Blue Book for Starsector ships.

Stat-Derived Ship Costs replaces static ship prices with values derived from hull stats, visible condition, market channel, and local economy context. Clean ships keep their prestige. D-modded ships actually sell like damaged goods. A battered cruiser can become a budget opportunity instead of somehow still costing almost full price. Highly tweakable with LunaLib with bands in-place to prevent mistakenly cheesing the ship market.

Download
GitHub

Requires:
LunaLib

Game Version:
Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Features:

Derives base ship value from hull stats instead of relying only on vanilla price entries.
D-mods strongly reduce ship value, with severity scaled by hull size.
S-mods have little face-value effect and mostly matter through the final ship stats.
Open Market, Military Market, and Black Market each have their own pricing behavior.
Selling prices are adjusted separately so markets behave more like buyers with motives, margins, and preferences.
Local economy context can influence ship prices.
Major economy levers are configurable through LunaLib.
Supports TriOS and Version Checker update detection.

Design Goal:
The goal is a more immersive ship economy. Damaged ships should feel like damaged assets, rare hulls should keep some prestige, and players should be able to buy into bigger hull classes through riskier, beat-up ships instead of every market listing feeling like a fixed sticker price.

Changelog:
Version 1.1.4
-Updated LunaLib's D-hull minimum from 4 to 1

Please reset the mod to defaults in LunaLib

Version 1.1.2
-Eliminated stale market prices, cross-market contamination, unnecessary repricing, and a potential memory-retention issue.
-Added full support for modular ships by pricing the core and attached modules from their actual stats.
-Fixed SHIP_WITH_MODULES hulls being mistakenly excluded from SDSC pricing.
-Improved modular storefront and codex pricing while removing ineffective fleet-wide refresh work.
-Updated Version Checker to use GitHub's live archive instead of the problematic recursive ZIP.

Version 1.0.5
-Toggle off restores original values.
-Hull specs now only store the stat-derived baseline.
-Transaction-specific market/D-mod adjustments remain transaction-time only.
-Removed the static submarket cache and full-economy reprice pass.

Version 1.0.3
- Prevents free player-storage transfers from being treated as ship sales and granting credits.

Version 1.0.2
- Makes cargo-update repricing change-aware so external market viewers such as Stellar Networks do not trigger repeated repricing when the ship roster is unchanged.
- Avoids creating submarket cargo from passive cargo-update callbacks; explicit market open, transaction, load, and settings-change paths still force pricing updates.

Version 1.0.1
- Registers `SDSCTransactionGuard` as a transient campaign listener so the mod can be removed from existing saves.
- Converts any previously persistent transaction guard instance to the transient form on load.
- Debounces cargo-update repricing to avoid external market UI modules triggering a reprice every frame.

Version 1.0.0
- Initial public release.
- Derives ship value from hull stats, visible D-mod condition, local market context, and market channel.
- Adds LunaLib settings for the major economy levers.
- Adds storefront pricing for open, military, and black markets.
- Adds sale-channel payouts and transaction protection against stale market-tab pricing.
- Writes hull value reports to `Starsector/saves/common/sdsc_hull_value_report.csv`.

discordPostHtml:
"The Kelly Blue Book of Spaceships"

The most important immersion mod for any modded Starsector run. Ships are no longer priced by vibes, they are appraised by their actual hull stats, condition, rarity, logistics burden, and market channel.

Stat-Derived Ship Costs acts like a Kelly Blue Book for spaceships. It evaluates loaded ship hulls and replaces arbitrary market prices with stat-derived values that better reflect what a ship is actually worth in the Sector.

Powerful ships are not nerfed. The economy simply recognizes them. If a ship is trash, the market will reflect that.

That sleek destroyer might still look amazing, but the ugly frigate you used to ignore may suddenly reveal itself as the better buy! Especially when you realize you can deploy three of them for the same DP cost.

Features:

  • Stat-derived ship hull pricing
  • Highly Tunable
  • Positive Faction Relations give dynamic discounts
  • D-mod condition pricing
  • Open, military, and black market unique price behavior
  • Rarity, logistics, and market-context adjustments
  • Hull value report generation
  • Designed for heavily modded games with inconsistent ship pricing
  • Will flip your logic when composing fleets

Save Compatibility Notice

Safe to add to an existing save.
Safe to remove, but ship prices will return to normal after the mod is disabled and the game is restarted.

A full restart is recommended after updating.

Download: https://github.com/Compterra/Stat-Derived-Ship-Costs/archive/refs/heads/main.zip
Forum Thread: https://fractalsoftworks.com/forum/index.php?topic=35645.0
